rationale: Claude's plan has the most coherent core (a single bind-once durable guidance snapshot read by buildOrder, ownerControls extraction without a second tick loop, AbortSignal quit, and TTY-injected terminal tests), and its reviewed gaps (fresh-batch identity on owner retry, a cancellable poll timer, a stop-intent guard before completion detach, and step/roster in the status snapshot) are localized fixes, whereas Cursor's per-prepare queue clearing breaks cohort consistency and Codex's multi-site promotion can discard guidance on no-action transitions.
